c01-1: His name is in the letter of assignment; his position is in a Hautcorvin register and in the press of 1889.
c01-2: Useful document: the photograph of the Glassworks' stand at the Grand Exhibition. The Reader brings it up on “Grand Exhibition” or “Tennok lens”.
c01-3: Back of the 1889 photograph: “É., C. and H.” The man has his spectacles pushed up on his forehead and a chinstrap beard, as in the garden in 1915.
c02-1: Her birth name is in the Hautcorvin registers; her occupation can be read in the Exhibition press.
c02-2: Useful document: the 1878 marriage, in the Hautcorvin registers.
c02-3: In the 1889 photograph, the woman wears a round brooch of gilded glass; the newspaper mentions a casket “gilded by Mrs Tessonnal herself”.
c03-1: This slot appears when you read who Andrin's grandfather was. His occupation is in the same certificate.
c03-2: Useful document: the photograph “Dalvica, 1916”, from the Honoré collection, brought up on “Dalvica” or “Dranko”.
c03-3: Translated caption of the 1916 photograph: “Dranko, Danela, Andrin”. The man in front of the charcoal clamp has the straight, thick eyebrows of the Dalvarins.
c04-1: The Vernezac birth registers name Jules Neviot's parents.
c04-2: Useful document: the photograph of the opening of the Refuge de l'Ourse (1911).
c04-3: 1911 caption: “Mr and Mrs B. Neviot”. The old man has a three-fingered hand on the handle of his shovel.
c05-1: She brought half of Vernezac into the world: look for who registered Andrin Dalvarin's birth.
c05-2: Useful document: the postcard of the Combe-aux-Sables (a midwife on her mule).
c05-3: “Annette Neviot, née Combal, midwife”: her birth name is in the 1912 certificate and in the Vernezac births.
c07-1: The petition and the objection both speak of his mother, without always naming her.
c07-2: Useful document: the 1904 marriage in the Hautcorvin registers; it gives her name and her occupation.
c07-3: In the 1928 wedding photograph, the lady with the velvet ribbon beside Honoré is the bride's mother; the back of the 1915 photograph names her “Eugénie”.
c08-1: The first hearing names her by her given name; her son's birth certificate, by her surname.
c08-2: Useful document: the photograph of the engraving workshop (1912), brought up on “engraving workshop”.
c08-3: “Miss D. Dalvarin, engraver”: dark eyes, straight, thick eyebrows, leather apron. You will find her again in Dalvica in 1916 and in 1955.
c09-1: Mind the name: a nun has a name in religion, but the Office registers her civil name.
c09-2: Useful document: the Vernezac baptism certificate (1912); it gives both of the godmother's names.
c09-3: “Marguerite Tessonnal, in religion Sister Agathe”: the nun in the cornette in the 1915 garden photograph.
c10-1: He is a witness at his brother's wedding in 1904, and godfather to a child in 1912.
c10-2: Useful document: the postcard of the Cap de Tennok (1911), from the Honoré collection.
c10-3: In the 1915 garden photograph, the standing man in round-rimmed spectacles carries a lens maker's round loupe.
c11-1: A guide, badge No. 7, and a father: look in the Vernezac births.
c11-2: Useful document: the photograph of the opening of the Refuge de l'Ourse (1911).
c11-3: 1911 caption: “the guide J. Neviot (No. 7) and Mrs Neviot”. Badge No. 7 is also on the back of the Combe postcard.
c12-1: She kept an inn: the 1926 directory lists her under her married name.
c12-2: Useful document: the Vernezac births, which give her birth name.
c12-3: In the 1911 photograph, the young woman with the checked apron and the bunch of keys is the wife of guide No. 7.
c13-1: The objection is signed in her name: you already have her given name, the surname she goes by and her position.
c13-2: Useful document: the 1928 wedding photograph, brought up on “Colombe Tessonnal” or “Studio Orlhac”.
c13-3: Her birth name is in the 1928 marriage register. The 1928 bride has her mother's dimple and grey eyes.
c14-1: Company secretary of the firm for thirty-two years, says the objection.
c14-3: The 1928 groom has a pencil-line moustache and a raised right eyebrow; you will find him again in 1958, at his daughter's wedding.
c15-1: The statement is a document like any other: cross-check it. Two declared fields do not hold.
c15-2: Useful documents: the 1938 arrest record (description) and Removal List No. 9 (position).
c15-3: Grey eyes, a cowlick, a burnt right hand: look for a photograph from before 1944 with his name written on it, the one of the 1936 walkout or the one of the St Éloi competition.
c16-1: Agnès Neviot's petition gives her mother's name and occupation.
c16-2: Useful document: the photograph of the 1947 wedding in Vernezac.
c16-3: The young woman with the black plait and the horn whistle: at the refuge in 1937, married in 1947, on the 1962 poster.
c17-1: The will speaks of a child who did not bear his father's name; the slot sits under Honoré and under a woman engraver.
c17-2: Useful document: the 1953 re-registration in Vernezac, with its identity photograph.
c17-3: Before 1944, two photographs show him beside the glassblower: straight, thick eyebrows, dark eyes, no cowlick, leather apron. It is the same face, younger, as the one on the petition.
c18-1: This slot appears when you read his marriage, or the 1938 arrest.
c18-2: Useful document: the 1947 wedding photograph (the groom in uniform).
c18-3: The 1947 groom is very tall, with sticking-out ears; do not confuse him with Sergeant Fauvel, who wears the same uniform.
c19-1: A guide like his father and like his son: look at the numbered badges.
c19-2: Useful document: the 1966 article on the Vernezac guides' roped party.
c19-3: Rémi wears badge No. 19; his son, No. 31; his father, No. 7.
c20-1: A schoolmistress in Vernezac, known by her married name.
c20-2: Useful document: the photograph of the 1947 class, brought up on “Vernezac school”.
c20-3: “Mrs Odette Neviot”, low bun, round spectacles, grey overall: her birth name is in the 1934 marriage.
c21-1: The objection names him, with his position.
c21-2: Useful document: the 1960 wedding photograph (Studio Orlhac).
c21-3: “Mr Hugues Brossal, engineer at the Glassworks”: pale eyes behind spectacles, a dimple, a bow tie.
c22-1: This slot appears with a marginal note in the Brossal register entry.
c22-2: Useful document: the 1960 wedding photograph, or the 1972 directory.
c22-3: “Miss Sabine Orlhac, of Studio Orlhac”: straight fringe, hoop earrings. In 1974, all you see is her reflection in a shop window.
c23-1: A journalist on the Sentinel; the objection names her by her married name.
c23-3: Her birth name is in the Brossal register entry; she signs the article “The Revenant of Hautcorvin”.
c24-1: He is the one who forwards Honoré's will.
c24-3: Two men with the same nose in the 1958 photograph: the groom has a short beard and half-moon spectacles; his father, a white moustache.
c25-1: Her 1974 petition gives her name and her occupation.
c25-2: Useful document: the article “The Revenant of Hautcorvin” (photograph with her half-brother).
c25-3: Grey eyes, a dimple, a cowlick in the middle of the forehead, a horn whistle: the same woman in 1974 at the Snow Festival.
c26-1: This slot appears with his mother's second marriage.
c26-2: Useful document: the January 1976 article on the revenant, or the 1974 Snow Festival.
c26-3: Sticking-out ears, a bobble hat, glacier glasses: the instructor from the ski school.
c27-1: A guide like his father: badge No. 31.
c27-2: Useful document: the 1966 article on the roped party.
c27-3: Black beard, woollen hat, ice axe, badge No. 31: on the 1966 roped party and at the 1974 Snow Festival.
c28-1: This slot appears with the 1941 Vernezac births, or with a telegram.
c28-2: Useful document: the 1972 directory (Vernezac post office).
c28-3: “B. Neviot, postmistress” endorses the telegrams; she is the one who spent the night at the telegraph in 1966.
g-revenant-1: The three slots are established together: the claimed slot, the “?” slot and the daughter. A face can only be placed once.
